description: Migrate all 29 function definition files in packages/inngest-functions/src/functions/ to use the new createFunction adapter from @oxagen/inngest-functions instead of directly calling inngest.createFunction(). Each file replaces its import of inngest with an import of the adapter, rewrites the definition to use the abstract interface, and the business logic in handlers remains unchanged.
steps: 1. Migrate the simplest event-triggered functions first as a pattern: chat.persist-stream.ts, stripe.sync-subscription.ts, stripe.sync-invoice.ts. Replace `import { inngest } from '../inngest'` with `import { createFunction } from '../create-function'`. Convert inngest.createFunction(config, trigger, handler) to createFunction(config, trigger, handler). The handler keeps its body unchanged but now receives the abstract {event, step} context.

2. Migrate cron-triggered functions: billing.rollup-usage.ts, billing.dunning-sweep.ts, plugin.catalog-sync-cron.ts, security.audit-partition-rollover.ts. These use { cron: '...' } triggers. Note: billing.rollup-usage.ts handler only destructures {step} (no event) - the adapter context always provides both, so this is safe.

3. Migrate functions with concurrency+cancelOn: agent.background-task.execute.ts, agent.workflow.supervisor.ts, agent.workflow.task.execute.ts. These use cancelOn config which maps directly to the abstract CancelOnConfig[].
4. Migrate functions with step.waitForEvent: agent.aggregate-fanout.ts. The abstract StepContext.waitForEvent matches Inngest's signature.

5. Migrate functions with step.sleep: privacy.erasure.execute.ts. Also uses NonRetriableError - change import from 'inngest' to import from '@oxagen/functions' (the adapter wrapper handles the translation).
6. Migrate functions with step.sendEvent: agent.execute-subagent.ts, ingestion.pipeline.ts, and others that call step.sendEvent.
7. Migrate the video-render function (agent.video-render.ts) which has timeouts config: { timeouts: { finish: '16m' } }. This maps to the new DurableFunctionConfig.timeouts field.

8. Migrate functions that have on-failure companions: agent.video-render.ts (agentVideoRenderOnFailure), privacy.erasure.execute.ts (privacyErasureExecuteOnFailure), privacy.export.process.ts (privacyExportProcessOnFailure). Convert these to use config.onFailure inline handler OR keep as separate createFunction calls with the failure trigger pattern - whichever preserves behavior better.

9. Migrate remaining functions: agent.sync-execution-to-graph.ts, auth.session-expiry-audit.ts, ingestion.delete.ts, ingestion.oauth-refresh.ts, ingestion.github-initial-sync.ts, ingestion.github-parse-file.ts, ingestion.github-infer-features.ts, ingestion.semantic-edge-infer.ts, ingestion.sync-requested.ts, playbook.trigger.match.ts, playbook.run.execute.ts, plugin.registry-sync.ts, plugin.oauth-refresh-watcher.ts.

10. Update packages/inngest-functions/src/functions.ts to import from the migrated files. If the adapter returns DurableFunction[] (to include on-failure companions), flatten the array in the functions registry.

11. Ensure apps/api/src/routes/inngest.ts still type-checks. The serve layer receives the functions array which is provider-native Inngest functions under the hood (the DurableFunction type is satisfied by what createFunction returns).

12. Update existing test files to work with the new pattern. The tests currently mock inngest.createFunction - they should now mock the adapter or test through it. Ensure all existing tests still pass.
acceptance_criteria: All 29 function files import createFunction from the adapter instead of inngest.createFunction directly
No function file imports from 'inngest' SDK directly (except through the adapter layer)
NonRetriableError is imported from '@oxagen/functions' in privacy.erasure.execute.ts and privacy.export.process.ts
The functions array in src/functions.ts still exports all 31 entries (29 primary + 3 on-failure companions) - or equivalent via flattening
All existing unit tests pass (may need mock updates)
findings: Migration successful. Key findings: (1) Tests that mock ../inngest to capture the handler needed to be updated to mock ../create-function instead, because the adapter wraps the handler and expects ctx.event to be an object. (2) Three files (agent.workflow.supervisor, ingestion.sync-requested, playbook.trigger.match) still import inngest from ../inngest because they call inngest.send() directly inside step.run blocks. (3) The functions registry needed a .filter(fn => fn != null) to handle the undefined from array destructuring of createFunction results (on-failure companion being the 2nd element). (4) The functions array type was changed to any[] to satisfy the inngestServe type constraint (DurableFunction interface does not have Symbol.toStringTag that Inngest's Like type requires, even though the runtime objects are valid Inngest functions).
